The predicted diagnosis dismisses any acute infectious or systemic illness, labels the finding as benign and self-limited, and recommends no further action unless new symptoms arise — which is fundamentally inconsistent with congenital rubella, a chronic, multisystem disorder requiring definitive diagnosis (e.g., IgM antibodies, PCR), specialist evaluation, and long-term follow-up. The prediction fails to recognize the diagnosis entirely and contradicts its established clinical significance.
